title: Isolation economics narrative for platform buyers
summary: Working draft: tactical messaging and procurement signals for selling dedicated GPU/reserved capacity to platform and infra buyers. Focus on how isolation + SLA guarantees translate into predictable latency, tail protection, and deterministic cost per inference for scaled LLM workloads.
primary_value_propositions: Guaranteed throughput and isolation to protect critical low-latency paths from noisy neighbors
SLA-backed latency targets with financial remedies mapped to business impact
Predictable per-token economics at scale via reserved capacity and smart routing
Operational simplicity vs managing on-prem GPU fleets (patching, kernel tuning, kernel selection)
supporting_evidence_points: Internal benchmark: 99.9th pct latency improvement under reserved pools vs shared in production test (customer X sim)
Prefix/KV cache effectiveness reduces burst token cost up to 40% when pinned to dedicated pools
Audit trail and token-level cost breakdowns for chargeback to product teams
Customer reference (anonymized): reduced cost variability and simplified SLA negotiations with infra procurement)
buyer_pain_signals_to_listen_for: Frequent production latency spikes during peak inference periods
Procurement pushback on variable monthly cloud bills for inference
Platform teams running their own GPUs and struggling with ops headcount
Need for isolation due to compliance or multi-tenant risk policies
common_objections_and_rebuttals: Objection: 'We can self-host cheaper.' => Rebuttal: provide TCO checklist (headcount, ops, MTTI, kernel tuning, model updates) and show break-even horizon; include risk of model regression without continuous kernel ops
Objection: 'We don't want vendor lock-in.' => Rebuttal: explain model/version pinning, canary and rollback policies, migration stories, and optional private deployment model
Objection: 'We need proof of SLA.' => Rebuttal: propose pilot with measurable SLOs, provide audit logs, and reference SLAs with financial remediation examples
procurement_scripting_and_playbook: Open: frame problem — 'Large language models are a new class of infra: variability costs money. Our reserved offering turns variability into a contractable guarantee.'
Quantify: 'At N qps and p tokens/request, your expected per-token cost swings by X% on shared pools; reserved reduces that swing to Y%.' (have calculator for ops)
Anchor: 'If latency is business-critical, dedicate capacity or buy a predictable throughput tranche — otherwise plan for spike spillover policies.'
Negotiation lever: offer dual-contract options (baseline reserved + burst pool) to meet procurement risk profiles
SLA ask template: specify 99.9th latency at target sequence length, average throughput per GPU, and remediation ladder (credit, accelerated capacity allocation, dedicated engineering escalation)
competitive_angles: Cloud vendors: cheaper raw GPUs but no tailored LLM kernel selection or prefix caching policies; higher ops burden
Self-hosted inference stacks: maximum control but hidden ongoing tuning costs and slower recovery windows
Other inference vendors: vary on observability and SLA granularity — position Redwood with token-level billing, route-level dashboards, and canary rollouts
procurement_playback_examples: Scenario A - Marketplaces/Customer-facing chat: needs 95th/99.9th latency guards — sell reserved baseline + burst capacity with 15% discount on committed usage
Scenario B - High-volume batch embeddings: emphasize throughput guarantees and cost-per-embedding smoothing via dedicated pools and intelligent batching suggestions
Scenario C - Regulated workloads: combine Dedicated with Private control plane and KMS integration as a single procurement package
pricing_anchors_and_metrics_to_share: Committed monthly GPU hours, effective tokens/hour, expected model family (e.g., Llama-3 medium vs 70B), buffer for burst (x% of baseline), and suggested amortized software/ops credit to show TCO delta vs self-hosting
slides_outline: Title + TL;DR: isolation = predictable business outcomes (latency & cost)
Why variability matters: short case study + numbers
What isolation buys you: technical + procurement impacts
TCO snapshot vs self-hosting + third-party clouds
Procurement options: baseline reserved, reserved+burst, private deployment add-on
Call to action: trial offer / prescriptive ROI calculator
open_questions_and_DECISIONS_needed: Define standard SLA numerics we can publish (sequence length assumptions, metric windows)
Decide default remediation ladder wording (credits vs other remedies)
Agree on pilot acceptance criteria and measurement tooling (traces, token-level billing exports)
Which anonymized customer references are okay to use in procurement decks? legal clearance needed

notes_to_self: Keep tone pragmatic; procurement teams want numbers and fail-open mitigations. Avoid overpromising model-level accuracy gains — focus on operational guarantees. Build a short checklist that maps product config (autoscaling, burst, KV caching) to procurement asks so AEs can 'fill in the blanks' quickly.
informal_brainstorm_snippets: 'Could we offer a 'latency insurance' add-on that pays credits when 99.9th violated? Good for legal buy-in'
'What if we pre-define a 'safe' model variant for reserved pools to ensure quantization and kernel selection stability?'
'Sales should highlight 'no finger-pointing' runbook vs self-hosting — one vendor responsible for ops & remediation'
auditable_artifacts_to_attach_for_pilot: benchmark report (pdf) comparing shared vs reserved under peak synthetic workload
tone_and_style_guidance: Voice: concise, numbers-first, and procurement-savvy. Use concrete anchors (percent improvements, dollars/100k tokens) where possible. Keep legal-friendly phrasing for SLA but include optional escalations for enterprise buyers.
